title: Slide Deck
summary: Slide deck editor for a short presentation: a slide list with live thumbnails, a 16:9 canvas where each slide is a layers document (title, body and image layouts; drag, scale, restyle and add text or shapes), an accent from the T3 theme, deck undo history, presenter mode that fills the frame, and export of every slide as a 1920x1080 PNG plus a JSON deck. Pick it for any slides, pitch, review or talk deck, or a presentation built from photos.

title.description: Header title and the export file prefix (slug): <title>-01.png ... and <title>.json.

body.description: One point per line (\n); long lines wrap.

image.description: File name of an attached image, e.g. horizon.jpg.

default.title: Sonoma Spring
default.body: Notes from one week in wine country

default.title: What We Saw
default.body:
Golden light over the vines
Long lunches under the oaks
A hillside at dusk

slides.description: Slides in order: { title, body?, image?, layout? }. Layout when omitted: image if an image is named, body if there is a body, else title. An image layout without an image uses the first attached image; a name that is not attached warns and leaves an empty image slot.

accent.description: Accent bar colour: a theme token (primary, chart-1..chart-6, info, success, warning), var(--token), or any CSS colour. Invalid values warn and use primary.

customScript.description: JS run last as (t3template, options) to bolt on controls, image stages, panels, buttons and a setValues path. See boltOn.

controls.description: Starting values for bolt-on controls, { controlId: value }, applied when customScript adds them (a saved edit wins). An id no control claims is an error.

boltOn.summary: options.customScript runs once as new Function('t3template', 'options', code), after the media has loaded, the first slide has rendered and the template's panels exist. Add controls, then image stages: they draw on every rendered slide picture (each exported PNG, the presenter and the slide-list thumbnails) after its layers render, so frames, grain, footers and slide numbers reach every exported file. Image stages do not repaint the editable canvas: check them in a thumbnail, Present (P) or Export. To change the slides themselves use setValues or instances.layers. Control values persist with the edit; options.controls ({ id: value }) sets starting values, and a saved edit wins over it. Errors log "[t3template] customScript error: ..." and show in a dismissible banner. Arrow, PageUp/PageDown and Home/End keys are also taken (slide list, presenter, layer nudge).
api: addControl({ id, label?, type: 'slider'|'toggle'|'select'|'color'|'text'|'button', min = 0, max = 1, step?, default?, options?: ['a', { value, label }], placeholder?, rows?, panel?: 'Title' | element from addPanel, onChange?(value, t3template), onClick?(t3template) }) -> { id, element, get(), set(value), setLabel(text) }. Values: slider number, toggle boolean, select the option value, color '#rrggbb', text string. No panel = 'Extras'. User edits and set() re-render the thumbnails and presenter; onChange runs on edits only. Every control edit is one undo step (a slider drag, a typing burst); undo, redo and history jumps restore control values with the deck.

addImageStage(id, (ctx, controls) => void): edits a rendered slide picture in place with ctx.context (2D; getImageData works). ctx = { canvas, context, width, height, scale, phase, index (0-based slide), count, slide (id), layout, copy(), random(seed?) }. width x height: 1920 x 1080 for export and the presenter, 384 x 216 for thumbnails. scale = width / 1920: multiply pixel sizes by it or size things as fractions of width. copy() -> a snapshot canvas (draw it back blurred for glows; never draw the canvas onto itself). random(seed?) -> seeded () => [0, 1), the same pattern on every render. phase = 'preview' (thumbnails, presenter) | 'export'. Only the 'image' target exists here (default).

addShaderStage(id, glsl, (controls, { width, height, scale }) => ({ u_name: number | boolean | [x, y(, z, w)] | '#rrggbb' })): GLSL ES 1.0 fragment shader on each rendered slide picture, stages in the order added; u_image, u_resolution, u_scale and varying v_uv (0,0 bottom left) are declared for you, declare your own uniforms.   removeStage(id).

addPanel(title | { title, open = true, position = 'top' }) -> the panel body element (append your own nodes; the same title returns the same panel). 'top' = first in the right inspector, above Slide, in creation order (in view on load); 'bottom' = after Shortcuts.

addToolbarButton(label, onClick(t3template), { shortcut?: 'g' | 'shift+g' | 'mod+g', title? }) -> button, in the header before Undo.   refresh() re-renders thumbnails and presenter (only for state a hook reads that is not a control).

export() -> Promise<{ files: [{ name, type, size, width?, height? }] }>: renders every slide as a 1920 x 1080 PNG (<slug>-01.png, <slug>-02.png ...) through the image stages plus <slug>.json ({ format: 'slide-deck', version, title, accent, width, height, slides (options.slides shape), scenes (layers documents) }), attaches and downloads each file, reports what it wrote; throws on failure.

getValues() -> { title, accent, current, slides: [{ layout, title, body, image }], controls }.   setValues({ slides?, current?, accent?, controls? }, label?) -> Promise<values>: strict (unknown keys, unattached image names and bad accents throw). slides replaces the whole deck (layouts rebuilt from content, moves reset) and selects slide 0; current selects a 0-based slide; accent recolours every accent bar. One undo step.

on('change', cb) -> off.   instances: { layers (the editable canvas of the current slide: get(), update(id, patch), addText(text, props), addShape(kind, props); template layer ids are title, body, accent, image, image-slot; user edits on it are deck undo steps, but programmatic calls are only saved with the next deck step, so follow them with setValues({ current: t3template.getValues().current }, label)), history }.
